title: Typed reviewer adapters with honest degradation
goal: Adversarial review works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, CLI command, or human reviewer, and the absence of a reviewer is an explicit recorded gap that blocks landing rather than a silent weakening.
scope: Use docs/prds/BANDIT-PRD-006-consumer-agnostic-bootstrap.md as source authority for the second PRD-006 slice after BANDIT-100 landed the project-profile dependency and BANDIT-104 resolved the intervening work-execute route bootstrap gap.
Define a typed reviewer adapter contract with initial adapter types openai_compatible, cli_command, and human.
Validate reviewer adapter entries from the project profile or generated reviewer config with type-specific required fields and actionable diagnostics.
Generate or preserve profile-driven reviewer scaffolding under .bandit/reviewers/ without hardcoding Bandit's own Local Qwen identity as the only possible reviewer.
Generalize the current Local Qwen review path so the existing .bandit/reviewers/local-qwen.json route continues to run unchanged as an openai_compatible adapter through bin/omlx-chat-completions.mjs.
Make an empty reviewers list an explicit bootstrap gap or no-reviewer state that blocks landing gates until a reviewer exists or the gap is explicitly dispositioned.
Add a human reviewer adapter path that produces or validates review evidence satisfying the same gate contract without pretending a model review ran.

Keep reviewer evidence, reviewer config, bootstrap gap state, and landing-gate decisions repo-native and explicit; no cockpit, cache, prompt, or generated profile output may become independent workflow authority.
out_of_scope: Do not add same-harness self-review defaults.
Do not change reviewer quality calibration, reviewer benchmark scoring, paid reviewer promotion thresholds, or recurring paid reviewer policy.

Do not add hosted reviewer services, telemetry, external reviewer service setup, paid/live reviewer routing, provider-pricing evidence, spend-class approval, public benchmark publication, or automatic policy promotion.
Do not change Local Qwen's authorized route away from .bandit/reviewers/local-qwen.json through node bin/omlx-chat-completions.mjs.

Do not implement harness-neutral AGENTS.md generation, harness shims, policy tiers, V0 Closeout Claude Code A/B Product-Value Trial work, local API, State Index, guarded browser actions, Trust Verifier cutover, old-gate replacement or wrapping, merge, push, deploy, public npm publish automation, credential handling, hosted update services, automatic self-update, installed global skill mutation, automation prompt mutation, dependency changes, lockfile changes, package-script changes, CI/release workflow changes, external repo mutation, claim authority, worktree lifecycle, or unrelated Phase 8 work.
Do not start RED evidence, implementation, review-loop evidence, landing evidence, UAT evidence, retrospective evidence, or closeout evidence during Repo PM Stage 1 formation.
acceptance_criteria: Each reviewer adapter type validates at init or profile/config load with type-specific required fields and diagnostics naming the offending field.
The existing Local Qwen review flow runs unchanged as an openai_compatible adapter using .bandit/reviewers/local-qwen.json and node bin/omlx-chat-completions.mjs.
A profile or config with reviewers: [] records an explicit no-reviewer bootstrap gap or no-reviewer state that land-check treats as blocking until dispositioned.
A human adapter produces or validates a review-evidence path that satisfies the same gate contract without claiming Local Qwen, CodeRabbit, or another model reviewer ran.
Reviewer adapter config and generated .bandit/reviewers/ files are data/config surfaces, not hidden workflow authority; landing gates still consume explicit review evidence and gap disposition.
Focused tests cover adapter validation, scaffold output, Local Qwen regression routing, empty-reviewer landing blockade, disposition unblock behavior, and human-reviewer evidence validation.

The implementation preserves CLI Authority, repo-native source-of-truth boundaries, Permanent Test Ownership Boundary, Bootstrap Model-Family Separation, authorized Local Qwen routing, and fail-closed reviewer evidence semantics.

The slice does not change reviewer benchmarking, paid reviewer routing, harness shims, policy tiers, Trust Verifier cutover, public publishing, dependencies, merge/push/deploy authority, external repo mutation, or unrelated Phase 8 product scope.
test_plan: Stage 2 Test Writer writes RED tests for openai_compatible, cli_command, and human adapter validation, including missing required fields and actionable diagnostic text.
Stage 2 Test Writer writes RED tests for profile-driven reviewer scaffold output under .bandit/reviewers/.
Stage 2 Test Writer writes a Local Qwen regression proving the current .bandit/reviewers/local-qwen.json route still invokes node bin/omlx-chat-completions.mjs as an openai_compatible adapter.
Stage 2 Test Writer writes a landing-gate test proving reviewers: [] or equivalent no-reviewer state blocks land-check until dispositioned.
Stage 2 Test Writer writes a human-adapter evidence test proving manual review evidence can satisfy the same gate contract without model-review claims.
Run focused reviewer-adapter, init/profile, Local Qwen routing, and landing-gate tests after implementation.

Run npm test if implementation touches shared CLI startup, profile parsing, reviewer commands, landing gates, bootstrap gaps, validation, risk classification, supply-chain gates, cockpit/session-context, or package scaffolding behavior.
Run node ./bin/bandit.mjs cockpit status --json and node ./bin/bandit.mjs session-context current --json after routing artifacts are updated.
Run CodeRabbit review and authorized Local Qwen review before landing, with honest provider-timeout/refusal evidence if allowed by the active stage policy.
clean_code_read_evidence: CLEAN_CODE.md was read on 2026-06-12 before creating this source spec and repairing BANDIT-101 Stage 1 formation. This slice must keep reviewer adapter validation, scaffold generation, Local Qwen route reuse, no-reviewer gap recording, human review evidence, landing-gate integration, diagnostics, and tests small and explicit; avoid hidden authority; preserve role boundaries; and avoid mixing harness shims, policy tiers, reviewer benchmark policy, paid/live routing, Trust Verifier cutover, merge/push/deploy, dependency, package-script, CI/release workflow, or unrelated Phase 8 behavior into this slice.

bootstrap_gaps: No open bootstrap gap blocks this PRD-006 reviewer-adapter slice.

Only one real in-house live OpenAI-compatible reviewer endpoint, Local Qwen, is available for live verification in this slice; additional endpoint diversity is out of scope unless Stage 4 evidence records a new bounded follow-up.
Live CodeRabbit formation or Stage 4 review may time out or be unavailable; do not claim a CodeRabbit pass without terminal evidence.

Local Qwen is authorized only through .bandit/reviewers/local-qwen.json and bin/omlx-chat-completions.mjs against the MLX OpenAI-compatible endpoint at http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1. If the endpoint or adapter is unavailable, stop and ask the operator for help rather than substituting another reviewer route.
first_implementation_order: Repo PM repairs or creates Stage 1 formation artifacts and approves formation before Work Item PM execution.
Work Item PM records plan-mode orchestration only after formation_approved and before RED evidence.
Test Writer writes failing tests for adapter validation, scaffold output, Local Qwen regression, no-reviewer landing blockade and disposition, and human adapter evidence.

Implementation Writer adds the minimal reviewer adapter validation, scaffold, Local Qwen route reuse, no-reviewer gap, human evidence, command wiring, and landing-gate integration needed to satisfy RED tests, without editing Test Writer-owned files if Codex authored the RED tests.
Codex PM verifies focused tests, typecheck, full tests as needed, Bandit validation, cockpit/session-context derived status, clean-code compliance, and evidence freshness before Stage 4 review.
Reviewers run Local Qwen through the authorized MLX route and CodeRabbit terminal evidence or policy-accepted provider-failure evidence; PM dispositions any findings before landing.
Landing Agent writes landing verdict/action; Closeout Agent records retrospective, improvement/no-action disposition, and synchronizes current context, roadmap, STATUS, and gap/intake state.
smell_triggers: Reviewer identity hardcoded outside .bandit/reviewers/ is a scope and clean-code warning unless explicitly limited to backwards compatibility.
A landing path that passes with zero review evidence and no dispositioned no-reviewer gap is a blocker.
Endpoint assumptions baked into review prompts, commands, or landing gates instead of typed adapter config are blockers.
Any direct qwen CLI, Ollama, paid/live reviewer, or ad hoc local reviewer route treated as Local Qwen evidence is a blocker.
Any CodeRabbit timeout, provider error, malformed output, missing route, missing operator-owned input, stale evidence, review blocker, or gate failure reported as pass evidence is a blocker.
Any implementation that lets reviewer config, generated templates, profile docs, cockpit/session-context output, or command output become canonical workflow authority is a blocker.
Any Implementation Writer edit to tests, test helpers, fixtures, RED evidence, acceptance mappings, or Test Writer-owned evidence is a blocker.

Any expansion into reviewer benchmarking, paid reviewer promotion, harness shims, policy tiers, Trust Verifier cutover, merge/push/deploy, dependencies, package scripts, lockfiles, CI/release workflows, hosted services, telemetry, public publishing automation, external repo mutation, installed global skill mutation, automation prompt mutation, claim authority, worktree lifecycle, or unrelated Phase 8 work is scope creep.

Any large mixed function that combines profile parsing, adapter validation, scaffold writes, review invocation, gap mutation, landing-gate parsing, evidence rendering, and diagnostics without small explicit boundaries is a clean-code blocker.

Halt for operator input if later work would approve paid or live reviewer/model routing, provider pricing, hosted services, telemetry, credential handling, public npm publish automation, automatic self-update, external repo mutation, installed global skill mutation, automation prompt mutation, merge/push/deploy authority, Trust Verifier cutover, old-gate replacement/wrapping, product or UAT direction changes, business tradeoffs, explicit cost/risk posture, or genuinely ambiguous scope.

continuation_decisions: CodeRabbit formation review must receive the full 600-second prompt-required timeout before any failed attempt is recorded.
Repo PM must retry CodeRabbit formation review up to two more times after a timeout and stop for operator assistance if all three attempts fail to produce terminal evidence.
Local Qwen unavailability is fail-closed and requires operator help rather than an alternate reviewer path.
Any paid, live, or recurring model/reviewer route remains blocked unless a separate approved provider-pricing and spend-class artifact exists.
